entries.title: International System of Units (SI)
entries.summary: Established following the May 20, 1875 Metre Convention, the SI defines seven base units (meter, kilogram, second, ampere, kelvin, mole, candela) and 22 named derived units. The 2019 SI redefinition (effective May 20, 2019) anchors every unit to seven defining physical constants.

places.note: Metre Convention signed in Paris; BIPM in Sevres

entries.title: Galileo's telescopic Moon observations (1609-1610)
entries.summary: In 1609-1610, Galileo Galilei turned an improved telescope skyward and published Sidereus Nuncius (1610), showing from shadow geometry across lunar craters and mountains that the Moon is not a smooth translucent sphere.

entries.title: Transistor effect discovery (1956 Nobel Prize)
entries.summary: The 1956 Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded jointly to William Bradford Shockley, John Bardeen, and Walter Houser Brattain for their semiconductor research and discovery of the transistor effect.

entries.title: Early relay and electronic computing (1939-1942)
entries.summary: Per the Computer History Museum timeline, landmark 1939-1942 machines included George Stibitz's Complex Number Calculator (1939, demonstrated remotely over telephone lines in 1940), Konrad Zuse's binary relay Z3 (1941), the Turing/Keen Bombe, and the Atanasoff-Berry Computer (1939-1942).

entries.title: Baikonur Cosmodrome

tiers.everyday: Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan is where the Soviet Union launched Sputnik, the first artificial satellite, on 4 October 1957. ESA says Yuri Gagarin's first human spaceflight left from here too.
tiers.student: NASA says Sputnik was launched from the Baikonur Cosmodrome on 4 October 1957. ESA says construction began in 1955 and that Yuri Gagarin's 12 April 1961 flight left from Launch Pad 1. The name came from a mining town about 370 km away, used to hide the real site.

entries.title: Kourou, Guiana Space Centre

tiers.everyday: Europe's Spaceport at Kourou in French Guiana is a launch base close to the equator. France chose the site in 1964, and the first launch from it was in 1968.
tiers.student: ESA says France picked Kourou in 1964 after weighing 14 other candidate sites, the first launch was a Véronique in 1968, and Ariane rockets have flown from there since 1979. At about 5°3′ N it is just over 500 km from the equator, which helps rockets flying east.

entries.title: Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center

tiers.everyday: Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in Gansu, China, was the country's first satellite launch site. China's first satellite, Dongfanghong-1, was launched from here on 24 April 1970.
tiers.student: China's space agency says the centre was started in 1958 and covers about 2,800 km². On 24 April 1970 a Long March 1 rocket carried Dongfanghong-1 into orbit, the centre's first satellite launch, which made China the fifth country to launch its own satellite.

entries.title: Vandenberg Space Force Base

tiers.everyday: Vandenberg Space Force Base in California began as an Army camp in 1941. Its first missile launch was in December 1958, and in February 1959 it launched Discoverer 1, which the base calls the first polar-orbiting satellite.
tiers.student: The Space Force says Camp Cooke was set up in 1941, passed to the Air Force in 1957 and was renamed Vandenberg Air Force Base on 4 October 1958. The first missile launch, a Thor, was on 16 December 1958 and Discoverer 1 followed on 28 February 1959. It became a Space Force Base on 14 May 2021.

entries.title: Cape Canaveral launch site

tiers.everyday: Cape Canaveral is a US launch site in Florida. NASA's catalogue lists it as the launch site of the Apollo 11 mission.
tiers.student: NASA's NSSDCA catalogue lists the launch site of the Apollo 11 Lunar Module's mission as Cape Canaveral, United States, on 1969-07-16. This entry is one generic point for the site and adds no local detail; the Apollo 11 entry covers the mission.

entries.title: Apollo 12 landing site (Moon)

tiers.everyday: Apollo 12 landed on the Moon on 19 November 1969 in Oceanus Procellarum. NASA lists the site at 3.013 S, 23.422 W on the Moon.
tiers.student: NSSDCA's Apollo table lists a launch on 14 November 1969, 7.75 hours of moonwalk time, a 1.35 km traverse and 34.35 kg of samples. Coordinates use the DE421 Mean Earth/Polar Axis frame.
